common_questions.prompt: How did this conversation come about?
common_questions.hint: First decide who started the contact. If the caller says the person called, wrote, reported, asked, or made a request first, such as "you contacted us", "your report", "your service request", or "your inquiry", choose the option that the person contacted them first, even when the call is about a problem. The out-of-the-blue problem option fits only when the caller started the contact to say something is wrong: a virus or a hack, suspicious or unauthorised activity, a debt or a fine, a legal case or an investigation, or a suspended or blocked account. A review, an update, a reminder, a pending software update, a change to settings, a balance, an invitation, or news about something the person already has is not a problem. An offer the person did not ask for is the offer option, or the won-or-selected option when they are told they were picked or pre-approved. If the caller says they noticed a problem the person is already having, choose that option. Options about where the person found the number fit only when the call says where. Options that say the person is calling fit only when the person rang the caller. Someone the person knows passing on news or an opportunity is a personal contact.
